blurb: Californian breed whose ears curl back from the face toward the back of the skull
description: The American Curl is a cat breed from California known for ears that curl backward: medium-sized, with a soft, silky long or short coat that is easy to keep.
answer: The American Curl is a cat breed from Lakewood, California, known for ears that curl back from the face due to a spontaneous mutation. It is a medium-sized cat with a soft, silky coat in longhaired and shorthaired versions.

body: In June 1981 stray cats appeared on the doorstep of the Ruga family in Lakewood, California. A black female named Shulamith gave birth to kittens with the same curled ears and is the ancestor of all American Curls. The breed was first exhibited at a cat show in 1986, TICA gave the longhaired Curl championship status in 1992, and in 1999 it became the first breed admitted to the CFA Championship Class with both longhair and shorthair divisions.

The American Curl is a medium-sized cat that does not reach maturity until two to three years of age; the reference data lists a weight of about 3 to 5 kg, and females are smaller than males. Kittens are born with straight ears that begin to curl within 48 hours and stop curling after about four months, when the base becomes firm and the tips stay flexible.
Both the longhaired and shorthaired varieties have soft, silky coats that lie flat against the body.
The source material gives little information on the American Curl's personality. Breed clubs describe its temperament in their standards, but individual cats vary.
The coat is known to be relatively low maintenance. Sources give no specific exercise guidance; regular play is a sensible general recommendation for any cat.

The curl gene is dominant. Unlike the Scottish Fold's ear mutation, which is linked to osteochondrodysplasia, a cat carrying two copies of the curl gene observed over two years showed no sign of abnormality. The available sources name no other breed-specific conditions; regular veterinary check-ups are recommended.

faq.q: Are American Curl kittens born with curled ears?
faq.a: No. Kittens are born with straight ears, which begin to curl within 48 hours and set in their final shape at about four months.

faq.q: How big does an American Curl get?
faq.a: It is a medium-sized cat; reference data lists about 3 to 5 kg, with females smaller than males.

faq.q: Does the American Curl have the same problems as the Scottish Fold?
faq.a: The curl mutation is different from the fold mutation, and a cat with two copies of the curl gene observed over two years showed no abnormalities.
